source.title: Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders
source.authors: F. Nooralahzadeh; Lea Bogensperger; C. Bluethgen; M. Krauthammer

record.tranche_reason: The study measures sparse, finding-specific channels in frozen 3D medical vision encoders, extending related representation questions to a different model and modality setting; it does not test toy superposition models.
record.gate_note: The reported top-K probe results and channel ablations bear on sparse finding representations in real encoders. Report-generation metrics and general classification comparisons do not measure the representation claim and are omitted. The paper cites superposition work as related background, not as a result.
record.test_reason: The study cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background. Its results are supervised probe AUROCs and channel ablations on final embeddings of two 3D CT vision encoders (Pillar-0, Merlin). It does not test toy networks, capacity competition, polysemantic neurons, SAEs or feature dimensionality. It does not study LLMs, which V4 names. With 18 or 30 labels against 512–1152 dimensions, there is no condition of more features than dimensions. The claim that labels are decodable from about 10 channels is a related construct (localization of supervised labels), not superposition, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that frozen 3D CT encoders store findings in sparse, causally selective channel subsets. They add that these subsets overlap partially among clinically related findings. They also find the probe recipe transfers across hospitals and backbones only when encoder and label anatomy match, and breaks down under anatomy mismatch (regime C). The abstract's 'score collapses' overstates the measured mean on-target drop of 0.006 AUROC.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised statistical probes to rank and read embedding coordinates in pretrained medical vision encoders, rather than training toy networks with controlled sparse features and measuring superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports anatomy/backbone mismatch as reducing transfer: Merlin chest-label AUROC is 0.733 on CT-RATE and 0.605 on RadChest-CT, compared with Pillar-0 cross-institution AUROC 0.686 on RadChest-CT. For the sparsity analysis, K=10 is selected on a disjoint Pillar-0 train holdout and then used for Merlin without separate tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: In frozen 3D CT vision encoders, supervised finding labels are linearly decodable from about 10 calibration-ranked embedding channels, matching full-D AUROC (0.798 vs 0.793). Zeroing those channels lowers on-target AUROC more than off-target (0.0060 vs 0.00003). Channels are shared among related findings: for example, channel 897 appears in several findings' sets, and Jaccard overlap is 0.43 for pancreas/spleen vs lower thorax.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pretrained medical vision encoders, clinically labelled concepts concentrate in small, partly shared subsets of embedding coordinates rather than spreading uniformly.

record.problems: The study itself notes higher-variance channel estimates for rare findings with few positive calibration examples. The reported core sparsity and ablation values have no uncertainty estimates stated in the text. Evidence concerns embedding coordinates in medical vision encoders, not neuron-level or SAE feature geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 reports per-finding top-10 and all-D AUROCs for 18 CT-RATE findings; these were not expanded into separate rows because the text provides aggregate top-K results and the per-finding table would add many rows without changing the version verdict. Report-generation and general classification rows were omitted because they do not measure sparse representation geometry.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity-dependent transition, no geometry analysis.
All: no capacity competition or analysis of polysemantic neurons.
All: no analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
All: no LLMs, no SAE or dictionary recovery, no measure of feature spreading across neurons.
All: no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Reader guessed tests/T3 with V4 supports; rejected. V4 concerns LLMs and feature spreading or SAE recovery, whereas this study probes supervised labels in vision-encoder embeddings. Row r5's subject is mislabeled (it is Merlin, not Pillar-0). The ablation effects are small in absolute terms, and no uncertainty is given for the sparsity or ablation numbers; the bootstrap CIs cover report generation only.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, overcomplete sparse-feature setup, near-orthogonal feature geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular toy-model geometry are tested.
Does not test capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemantic neurons.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Tests sparse finding information in frozen 3D medical vision encoders, not LLMs; it does not use or evaluate SAEs/dictionary recovery, neuron-level feature spreading, or feature completeness.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional superposed feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Fit CCP using the top 1 calibration-ranked embedding channel per finding; report mean test AUROC across 18 CT-RATE findings.
rows.note: The paper reports a sharp rise from top-1 to top-10; one channel per finding recovers less performance than the top-10 result.
rows.check: Probe AUROC for a supervised label using the top-1 channel, in a vision encoder, not an LLM. It does not measure feature spreading, superposition or SAE recovery.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Fit CCP using the top 10 calibration-ranked embedding channels per finding; report mean test AUROC across 18 CT-RATE findings.
rows.note: The paper says top-10 matches full-dimension AUROC using 10 coordinates per finding.
rows.check: Top-10 probe AUROC (0.798 vs full-D 0.793). This is label decodability in a vision encoder and says nothing on V4's LLM claim. K=10 was itself selected as the smallest K within 0.005 of full-D.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Fit CCP using the top 50 calibration-ranked embedding channels per finding; report mean test AUROC across 18 CT-RATE findings.
rows.note: The paper reports performance saturating by top-50.
rows.check: Top-50 probe AUROC in a vision encoder. It does not measure what any version names.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Measure full-D CCP mean test AUROC across 18 CT-RATE findings.
rows.note: Reference result for comparing sparse top-K probes with the full embedding.
rows.check: Full-D reference AUROC (0.793). This is a baseline for the other rows, not a result, and has no baseline of its own.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Fit CCP-10 on the calibration split and evaluate abdominal-finding probes on the test split.
rows.locator: Transfer across datasets, backbones, and anatomy, Table 4 / Scenario (B)
rows.note: The study applies the same K=10 sparse-channel probe recipe to the frozen Merlin encoder.
rows.check: Subject is wrong: this is the Merlin encoder (D=512) on abdominal CT, not Pillar-0. It is also a classification performance value for the study's own method (with an AUROC 0.839, not compared to full-D), so it is not a representation measure.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Zero each source finding's calibration-ranked top-10 channels, then recompute held-out probe AUROCs; report the mean on-target AUROC drop.
rows.measure: Mean on-target AUROC drop after ablation
rows.locator: Analysis and discussion, Causal ablation; Fig. 3 description
rows.note: The paper reports this as approximately 20 times the off-target drop.
rows.check: Ablation selectivity of supervised probe channels in a vision encoder. The absolute on-target drop is tiny (0.0060 AUROC), despite the abstract's word 'collapses'. It does not bear on superposition.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: After zeroing a source finding's top-10 channels, measure the mean AUROC drop for other findings.
rows.measure: Mean off-target AUROC drop after ablation
rows.locator: Analysis and discussion, Causal ablation; Fig. 3 description
rows.note: The paper reports some elevated off-diagonal effects among clinically related findings, indicating partial circuit overlap.
rows.check: Off-target ablation drop (0.00003); a comparator for r6. Same issue: it does not measure any version's construct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Frozen 3D medical vision encoders, including Pillar-0 on CT-RATE and Merlin on abdominal CT
reader_labels.reason: Sparse top-10 channel probes retain full-embedding-level or strong finding prediction, and ablations selectively reduce target scores (r2, r5, r6, r7).
